title: Engineering Ergodicity-Breaking and Stable Emergent Conservation Laws in a Generic Quantum Many-body System Under Strong Periodic Drive
authors: Sagnik Chaudhuri, Anirban Das, Asmi Haldar, Arnab Das
abstract: A periodically driven quantum many-body system is believed to approach a locally infinite-temperature-like state as dictated by the ergodicity hypothesis, when all the couplings/parameters are of the same order. When the drive is stronger than a threshold value, a large class of systems is shown to break this mandate, exhibiting Dynamical Freezing (DF): ergodicity is broken due to the emergence of local operators with permanent memory of their initial values (PRX 11, 021008, 2021). However, an exception to DF has recently been noted in a particular setting (PRX 16, 011041, 2026). Here we identify the condition for ergodicity-breaking in a system under strong drive, and show how to stabilize DF by exact, local engineering. We further show that the Floquet Hamiltonian $H_{eff} = (i/T)\ln{[U(T)]}$ is non-local when ordered by spin-flips, in a non-DF system, while it turns quasi-local under our simple, local DF engineering that keeps the Hamiltonian $H(t)$ still non-integrable at each $t$. This perplexing non-universality is absent in equilibrium, where non-integrability is believed to imply ergodicity and thermalization universally. Our work paves a way to engineering novel ergodicity-broken interacting Floquet phases of matter in various quantum platforms, and also endows DF-assisted quantum error mitigation and state stabilization techniques (see Nature 653, 1027 (2026)) with unprecedented versatility and flexibility.
summary: This theoretical work develops methods to engineer stable, non-thermalizing quantum phases in periodically driven many-body systems. By identifying a necessary condition—that the effective Hamiltonian's time-independent part must be X-only—the authors propose specific local modifications to the system Hamiltonian or drive. These engineering techniques successfully stabilize dynamical freezing and ensure the effective dynamics remain quasi-local, offering a pathway to control quantum information flow.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of engineering stable ergodicity-breaking (EB) phases and emergent conservation laws in quantum many-body systems subjected to strong periodic driving.
main_result: Local engineering of the system's Hamiltonian or drive operator can stabilize Dynamical Freezing (DF) by enforcing a specific X-only structure on the effective time-independent part of the Hamiltonian, leading to a quasi-local effective Floquet Hamiltonian.
method: The analysis combines Floquet theory, the construction of an effective Hamiltonian ($H_{	ext{eff}}$), and diagnostic tools like long-time autocorrelation functions and the Frobenius norm applied to spin-flip ordered series.
model_or_system: The study uses generic quantum many-body systems, often modeled by spin chains (e.g., Ising-type models $H_1, H_2, H_3$), subjected to time-periodic driving $H(t)$. The dynamics are analyzed in the rotating frame.
key_observables: Normalized long-time-averaged autocorrelation of local operators ($m_x$), and the weight of spin-flip sectors ($\lVert H(\xi)_{	ext{eff}} Vert$) of the effective Hamiltonian.
important_parameters: Strong drive amplitude ($AD$), the threshold for ergodicity breaking, and the Hamming distance ($\xi$) used to probe the locality of $H_{	ext{eff}}$.
main_assumptions: The core conjecture is that stable EB requires the time-independent part of the rotating frame Hamiltonian ($V_0$) to be composed exclusively of X operators. Quasi-locality is assumed to be sufficient for stable, non-thermalizing dynamics.
figures_summary: Figures compare autocorrelation functions showing memory retention (stable EB) versus decay (unstable DF). They also plot the weight of spin-flip sectors ($\lVert H(\xi)_{	ext{eff}} Vert$) to demonstrate that engineered protocols suppress large-$\xi$ weight, indicating quasi-locality.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the problem of strong driving leading to ergodicity breakdown, introduces the criterion for stable EB ($V_0$ must be X-only), details two engineering routes (time-independent and drive modification), and finally verifies the success of these engineering methods by showing the resulting $H_{	ext{eff}}$ is quasi-local.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete, engineering-based mechanism to control fundamental quantum dynamics (thermalization vs. localization) in periodically driven systems, which is highly relevant for designing quantum simulators or robust quantum memories.
